extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting long or short papers to EMNLP 2026 (NLP researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation/acceptance expectations for submitting long or short papers to EMNLP 2026 via ACL Rolling Review (ARR), including topical scope, integrity and ethics policies, review process, formatting/page limits, and presentation/commitment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial, original, and unpublished research
rubrics_metrics.description: EMNLP 2026 invites submission of long and short papers featuring substantial, original, and unpublished research on empirical methods for Natural Language Processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to traditional research results, papers may contribute negative findings, survey an area, announce the creation of a new resource, argue a position, report novel linguistic insights derived using existing computational techniques, and reproduce (or fail to reproduce) previous results. Some accepted presentations may be of papers accepted by TACL and CL journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant topics / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be within the broad technical program; relevant topics include (but are not limited to) a long list of NLP areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics enumerated on the CFP: Clinical and Biomedical Applications; NLP and Code Models; Computational Social Science and Cultural Analytics; Dialogue and Interactive Systems; Discourse and Pragmatics; Efficient Methods for NLP; Ethics, Bias, and Fairness; NLP and Symbolic Reasoning; Generation; Human-Centered NLP and Human-AI Interaction; Information Extraction; Information Retrieval and Text Mining; Interpretability and Analysis of Models for NLP; Language Modeling; LLM Agents; Linguistic Theories, Cognitive Modeling, and Psycholinguistics; Machine Learning for NLP; Machine Translation; Multilingualism and Cross-Lingual NLP; Multimodality and Language Grounding to Vision, Robotics and Beyond; NLP Applications; Phonology, Morphology, and Word Segmentation; Question Answering; Resources and Evaluation; Semantics: Lexical and Sentence-Level; Sentiment Analysis, Stylistic Analysis, and Argument Mining; Speech Recognition, Text-to-Speech and Spoken Language Understanding; Summarization; Syntax: Tagging, Chunking and Parsing. Use this list to assess topical fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special theme: New Missions for NLP Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers for the EMNLP 2026 special theme should articulate, test, and advance visions for NLP in the era of large language models, addressing what the missions of NLP research are now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions may be empirical, theoretical, position, or survey papers, but should be grounded in clear claims, strong evidence, and actionable insights. Suggested theme subtopics include: rethinking progress and evaluation in NLP (beyond leaderboards, real-world impact, robustness, longitudinal behavior), moving from models to systems and ecosystems (agentic workflows, tool use, human experiences, organizational/ecosystem interactions), scientific understanding of language and cognition (using models as experimental instruments), data as a bottleneck and responsibility (data scarcity, contamination, synthetic data feedback loops, documentation/governance/consent), and LLMs as research tools (rigorous studies of their use in research processes without eroding standards). The theme is intended to complement breadth, encouraging ambitious but concrete work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Long Papers: 8 pages; Short Papers: 4 pages (for ARR submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final versions of accepted papers will be given one additional page of content (up to 9 pages for long papers, up to 5 pages for short papers) to address reviewers’ comments. Authors should use the provided templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow ARR submission requirements (referenced policies)
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must follow ARR submission requirements, which are referenced on the CFP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CFP explicitly lists following ARR requirements: Instructions for Two-Way Anonymized Review; Authorship; Citation and Comparison; Multiple Submission Policy; Resubmission Policy; Withdrawal Policy; ACL’s Publication Ethics Policy; ARR’s Ethics Policy including the responsible NLP research checklist; ACL’s Disclosure Policy; Limitations; Writing Assistance; Paper Submission and Templates; Optional Supplementary Materials. Authors must consult those linked policies and comply with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way anonymized (double-blind) review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing will continue to be double-blind: reviewers will not see authors, nor will authors see reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARR instructions for two-way anonymized review must be followed. The CFP notes there is no anonymity period requirement. ARR reviews will not be made publicly visible, though authors may optionally make their anonymized submitted articles publicly visible via ARR.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARR two-stage review and commitment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: EMNLP uses ARR as the reviewing system; submissions receive ARR reviews and meta-reviews, and then authors commit reviewed articles to a venue (e.g., EMNLP) where SACs and Program Chairs make final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process: (1) Authors submit to ARR and receive reviews and meta-reviews from ARR reviewers and action editors; (2) Authors commit reviewed articles to a publication venue via the OpenReview platform; EMNLP then decides based on ARR reviews/meta-reviews. After a paper has been fully reviewed, authors may commit to a conference or revise and resubmit for another round. At ARR submission time authors are asked to select a preferred venue used only to calculate acceptance rates (see binding policy for May 2026 cycle).

rubrics_metrics.name: ARR 2026 May submission policy binding for EMNLP
rubrics_metrics.description: For the ARR 2026 May cycle authors must explicitly declare which conference they intend to commit to at submission time; this choice is binding for EMNLP 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARR 2026 May submissions that do not select EMNLP 2026 during submission will not be able to commit to EMNLP 2026. This policy does not apply to submissions reviewed in prior ARR cycles that wish to commit to EMNLP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship rules during commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: During the commitment phase, it is not allowed to modify the author list (i.e., addition/deletion of authors is not allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modification of author order is possible. Adhere to ARR/Authorship policy in all other respects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions prohibition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the ARR Call for Papers for details. Papers must be submitted, at latest, by the ARR 2026 May cycle if intending to commit to EMNLP via that cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper integrity policies (unethical submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: EMNLP will act against unethical paper submissions that overwhelm community resources, including but not limited to thinly sliced contributions, submissions with hallucinated citations, and entirely AI-generated papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI writing assistance is permitted, but submissions that violate ACL Policy on Publication Ethics may be desk rejected, and all authors involved may be ineligible to commit their paper(s) to EMNLP 2026 and EMNLP 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reviewing workload and author reviewer registration
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are expected to sign up to review or serve as an Area Chair or Senior Area Chair, with assignments based on qualifications; after submission, all authors must complete the author registration form by May 27, 2026 EoD AoE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you receive assignments, reviews must be completed by July 6, or meta-reviews by July 29. In emergencies, chairs should be warned via the emergency declaration form. Exemptions are detailed in the ARR Author Reviewer Exemption Policy Page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for highly irresponsible reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly irresponsible reviewers may be ineligible to (re-)submit or commit their work during the next ARR cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting authors should ensure all coauthors are aware of this policy and that everyone on their team submits (meta-)reviews on time and according to guidelines. See ARR incentives link for definition/details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation requirement for accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: All accepted papers must be presented at the conference to appear in the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference will include both in-person and virtual presentation options. Papers without at least one presenting author registered by the early registration deadline may be subject to rejection. Long and short papers will be presented orally or as posters as determined by the program committee. Short papers will be distinguished from long papers in the proceedings, but there will be no distinction in the proceedings between papers presented orally and as posters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional supplementary materials and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit optional supplementary materials and must use the provided paper templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Paper Submission and Templates guidance on ARR/OpenReview; supplementary materials should respect the policies on anonymity and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible NLP research checklist, disclosure, limitations, and writing assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must adhere to ethics and transparency requirements: ARR’s Ethics Policy including the responsible NLP research checklist, ACL’s Disclosure Policy, Limitations statements, and Writing Assistance disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure checklists, disclosures, limitations, and any use of writing assistance are included according to the linked policies. Noncompliance may affect desk rejection or other actions under publication ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI Reviewing Experiment (opt-in)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program committee will run an opt-in AI Reviewing Experiment to collect feedback from authors on the utility of AI Reviewers in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI Reviews for opted-in submissions will not inform any part of the conference decision process. The experiment will run under IRB approval, using open-weights models on in-house compute or closed models that guarantee zero-data retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: No anonymity period requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Following ACL and ARR policies, there is no anonymity period requirement for EMNLP 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may choose to make their anonymized submitted articles publicly visible through ARR if they wish; otherwise ARR reviews are not made public.
